title: רבי זכאי

paragraphs: Rabbi Zakkai, whose students asked why he lived so long. He said he never urinated within four cubits of prayer, never gave his fellow a nickname, and never neglected sanctifying the day. His elderly mother sold her headscarf to buy kiddush wine. At her death she left 300 jars of wine; at his death he left his sons 3000 jars: chapter Benei Hair 27b. It appears he was Rabbi Yochanan’s father; his son Yochanan likewise lived 120 years, for a father bestows the natural span of his years on his righteous son. But this requires examination: Yochanan is called ben Zakkai, not ben Rabbi Zakkai. See shortly below, where I write that it appears this Rabbi Zakkai was not Yochanan’s father.
